description: Screens every ticker with a SQL `WHERE` clause and returns the matches. Run it now, or add `asof` to backtest it on any past date. The `q` grammar is a flat SQL WHERE over signal names: AND/OR/NOT, comparisons, numeric and string literals, custom signals by name. No JOIN or subqueries. With `group_by` the result is rollup rows, not tickers. Example: `gap_up AND market_cap < 2000000000 AND NOT earnings_this_week`.

asof.description: Target moment as `YYYY-MM-DD` (that day's close) or an ISO timestamp (that intraday moment; daily-only signals then carry the previous session's close, never that day's): the same read as it stood then, unlimited depth. In `q`, `now()` and `current_date` mean that moment, so `last_earnings_date >= now() - interval '7 days'` backtests as written. Full contract under As of a past date.

cursor.description: The previous response's `next_cursor`. Send it with the same params as the first page (`limit` may change); a page whose params differ is a 400 naming the param. Row scans only.

grain.description: Only with `asof`. Grain the past state is read at: `1m`, `1h`, `1d` or `auto` (default). `auto` blends: each signal comes from its freshest grain at or before the instant (minute, then hourly, then the last closed daily session), so nothing is refused for grain and no ticker is dropped; `_meta.blended` and `_meta.grains_present` say what contributed. Pin a grain for the fastest response: one grain is read instead of three, and every ticker is captured on the same clock. A signal the pinned grain does not store is a `400 interval_unavailable` naming the grains that carry it (`rsi_14`, fundamentals and valuation ratios are `1d`-only). `1m` and `1h` need a timestamp `asof`; with a bare date they are a `400 interval_unavailable`.

group_by.description: Groups the scan: 1–6 group keys (signals, expressions or one of your custom signals as a boolean key). Results become rollups in `results`, each carrying its keys. Name a key with `AS` to choose its JSON key (`market_cap > 1e11 AS mega`); an un-named expression is named for you. Default `select`: the keys + `COUNT(*) AS tickers`. Works with `asof`; does not paginate.

having.description: Only with `group_by`. Filter the rollups. Custom signals are valid here too.

limit.description: Page size. Max 100. Grouped scans do not paginate: `truncated: true` when groups were cut, so sort with `order` to keep the ones you want.

order.description: Signal to sort by; it joins the default row. On a grouped scan the default is the count alias `tickers` (or, with a custom `select`, the last item's alias, so alias it with `AS`), sorted NULLS LAST with the group keys as tiebreak.

q.description: SQL WHERE expression. Max 4000 chars; semicolons, comments and write keywords are rejected. Your custom signals are valid here: each expands to its SQL at run time. To scan named tickers: `ticker IN ('AAPL', 'MSFT')`; to scan one asset class: `asset_class = 'crypto'`.

select.description: What each result carries, as in SQL. Omitted: the default row (ticker, name, asset_class, asset_type, price, change_1d_pct, gap_pct, relative_volume, market_cap) plus every signal used in `q` and `order`; a custom signal appears as its own value, and a cross-ticker reference (`SPY.sma_50`) is not added. A list: exactly those items, `ticker` always included; expressions with `AS` work (`price / sma_50 AS dist`) and are validated like `q`. `*`: every signal in the catalog. All aggregates (`count(*), avg(rsi_14)`) without `group_by`: one summary row, in `results`. With `group_by`, each item is an aggregate or a group key. Aggregates: count/avg/sum/min/max/stddev/string_agg/bool_and/bool_or, plus `FILTER (WHERE …)`.

universe.description: Scope to a built-in universe (`top_10`, `top_100`) or one of your own, by id. An unknown one answers 200 with no results and its id in `not_found`. Omitted, the screen runs across every ticker.

name: tickerbot_scan
